title: Paschen-Back Effect in Atomic Spectra
short_intro: The Paschen-Back effect is the splitting of spectral lines in a strong external magnetic field where the magnetic interaction energy significantly exceeds the internal spin-orbit coupling energy. In this regime, the orbital and spin angular momenta decouple from each other and precess independently about the direction of the external magnetic field.

exam_scope.tgt_core: Basic definition of the effect, comparison with the normal and anomalous Zeeman effects, distinction between weak and strong field regimes based on internal vs external magnetic interactions, and the lifting of spatial degeneracy.
exam_scope.pgt_extension: Detailed quantum mechanical derivation of energy shifts using first-order perturbation theory, evaluation of matrix elements for weak vs strong fields, selection rules for transitions (delta m_l = 0, +-1 and delta m_s = 0), and calculation of shifted frequency intervals.

prerequisites: Vector model of the atom and space quantization
Spin-orbit coupling and fine structure of hydrogen-like atoms

concept_notes.heading: Condition for Paschen-Back Effect
bullets: The external magnetic field B must be extremely strong, such that the magnetic interaction energy (mu_B B) is much greater than the internal spin-orbit interaction energy (Delta E_so).
Under this condition, the internal coupling between orbital angular momentum L and spin angular momentum S is broken.
Both L and S become uncoupled and independently precess around the direction of the external magnetic field.

concept_notes.heading: Decoupling of L and S
bullets: In the weak-field Zeeman effect, L and S couple to form total angular momentum J, which then precesses around B.
In the Paschen-Back effect, L and S precess independently, meaning their z-components m_l and m_s are separately quantized along the magnetic field direction.
The total magnetic quantum number becomes m = m_l + m_s.

concept_notes.heading: Splitting Pattern and Simplification
bullets: The complex anomalous Zeeman pattern simplifies in the Paschen-Back regime to a normal triplet pattern.
The energy shift depends on the sum of the orbital magnetic quantum number and twice the spin magnetic quantum number.
Because m_s can take values like +1/2 and -1/2, each Zeeman component splits into doublets or multiplets depending on spin states, though many lines coalesce.

concept_notes.heading: Selection Rules
bullets: The selection rules for transitions in the Paschen-Back regime are delta m_l = 0, +-1 and delta m_s = 0.
Since delta m_s = 0, spin does not flip during the optical transition.
The resulting spectrum typically consists of three main groups of lines corresponding to delta m_l = 0, +-1, mimicking the normal Zeeman effect.

derivations.title: Energy Shift Calculation in the Paschen-Back Effect
derivations.conditions: Strong external magnetic field B directed along the z-axis, where magnetic interaction >> spin-orbit interaction.
steps: Write the Hamiltonian of the atom in a magnetic field as H = H_0 + H_so + H_B, where H_0 is the unperturbed Hamiltonian, H_so = A L \cdot S is the spin-orbit term, and H_B = \frac{\mu_B}{\hbar} (L + 2S) \cdot B is the magnetic interaction term.

Treat H_B as the dominant perturbation compared to H_so, or evaluate matrix elements in the uncoupled basis |n, l, m_l, m_s>. Energy shift due to magnetic field is Delta E_B = \langle m_l, m_s | H_B | m_l, m_s \rangle.
Substitute H_B into the expectation value using B along the z-axis: Delta E_B = \mu_B B (m_l + 2m_s), noting \langle L_z \rangle = m_l \hbar and \langle S_z \rangle = m_s \hbar.
Include the first-order perturbation correction due to spin-orbit coupling as a diagonal matrix element of A L \cdot S \approx A m_l m_s.
Combine terms to get the total energy expression including both magnetic and first-order spin-orbit contributions.
derivations.result: Delta E = \mu_B B (m_l + 2m_s) + A m_l m_s

derivations.title: Frequency Shift of Spectral Lines
derivations.conditions: Transition between an upper state (1) and lower state (2) in the Paschen-Back regime.
steps: Express the frequency of the emitted or absorbed radiation as \nu = \nu_0 + \frac{\Delta E_1 - \Delta E_2}{h}.
Substitute the energy shifts for both states: \Delta E_1 = \mu_B B (m_{l1} + 2m_{s1}) and \Delta E_2 = \mu_B B (m_{l2} + 2m_{s2}).
Apply the selection rules: delta m_s = 0 (implying m_{s1} = m_{s2}) and delta m_l = m_{l1} - m_{l2} = 0, +-1.
Factor out the common terms to find the frequency displacement from the unperturbed central frequency \nu_0.

graphs_and_experiments.title: Transition from Anomalous Zeeman to Paschen-Back Effect
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: A plot of energy levels (vertical axis) versus magnetic field strength B (horizontal axis), showing complex overlapping splitting at intermediate fields and a transition to straight, equidistant parallel lines at very high B fields.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: Illustrates how individual levels reorganize as the magnetic field overcomes internal spin-orbit coupling, leading to decoupling of L and S.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Frequently asked in conceptual multiple-choice questions regarding the behavior of spectral splitting as magnetic field strength increases.

graphs_and_experiments.title: Spectral Line Pattern Comparison
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: Three spectral line spectra side by side: (a) Zero field single line, (b) Anomalous Zeeman multiplet (complex), (c) Paschen-Back triplet (resembling normal Zeeman effect with hidden doublets).
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: Demonstrates that strong magnetic fields restore a simple triplet structure because terms with identical m_l shifts group together.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Tested via identification of spectral patterns under varying magnetic field strengths.

graphs_and_experiments.title: Vector Model of Atom in Paschen-Back Regime
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: Vectors L and S precessing independently and rapidly around the external magnetic field vector B along the z-axis, rather than precessing around a common total angular momentum vector J.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: Visualizes the independent quantization of L_z and S_z along the magnetic field axis.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Used in theoretical questions explaining spatial quantization in strong magnetic fields.

solved_numericals.question: Calculate the magnitude of the Bohr magneton given electronic charge e = 1.6 x 10^-19 C, Planck constant h = 6.63 x 10^-34 J s, and electron mass m_e = 9.1 x 10^-31 kg.
solution_steps: Recall the formula for Bohr magneton: \mu_B = \frac{e \hbar}{2 m_e} = \frac{e h}{4 \pi m_e}.

solved_numericals.question: In the Paschen-Back effect for a particular atomic transition, an electron transitions from a state with m_l = 1, m_s = +1/2 to m_l = 0, m_s = +1/2 in a magnetic field of 2.0 T. Find the energy shift of the upper state in Joules.
solution_steps: Identify the formula for energy shift in the Paschen-Back effect: \Delta E = \mu_B B (m_l + 2m_s).
Substitute the upper state quantum numbers: m_l = 1, m_s = +1/2, and magnetic field B = 2.0 T.
Compute the term inside parentheses: m_l + 2m_s = 1 + 2(0.5) = 1 + 1 = 2.

solved_numericals.question: Determine the frequency shift (in Hz) for the transition where delta m_l = +1, given a magnetic field B = 1.5 T and Planck's constant h = 6.63 x 10^-34 J s.
solution_steps: Use the frequency shift formula in the Paschen-Back effect: \Delta \nu = \frac{\mu_B B}{h} \Delta m_l.
Substitute the values: \mu_B = 9.27 \times 10^{-24} \text{ J/T}, B = 1.5 \text{ T}, \Delta m_l = 1, and h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34} \text{ J s}.

assumptions_and_limitations: Assumes the external magnetic field is sufficiently uniform across the radiating atoms.
Neglects nuclear spin interactions (hyperfine structure) which would introduce further small splittings.
Valid only in the strong-field limit where the magnetic interaction energy greatly exceeds the internal spin-orbit coupling energy.

common_misconceptions.wrong: The Paschen-Back effect produces the exact same splitting pattern as the normal Zeeman effect in all aspects.
common_misconceptions.correct: While it resembles a triplet like the normal Zeeman effect, each component actually consists of multiple unresolved lines because individual m_s states still contribute to the total energy shift.
common_misconceptions.why: Although selection rule delta m_s = 0 yields a triplet-like main structure, individual levels retain dependence on m_s.

common_misconceptions.wrong: In the Paschen-Back effect, total angular momentum J remains a good quantum number.
common_misconceptions.correct: Total angular momentum J is not a good quantum number in the Paschen-Back regime because L and S decouple.
common_misconceptions.why: The strong external field breaks the internal L-S coupling, making m_l and m_s separately conserved instead of j.

common_misconceptions.wrong: The Paschen-Back effect occurs at very low magnetic field strengths.
common_misconceptions.correct: Low magnetic field strengths produce the anomalous Zeeman effect, whereas the Paschen-Back effect requires extremely high magnetic fields.
common_misconceptions.why: The external magnetic energy must overcome the internal spin-orbit interaction energy.

quick_revision: The Paschen-Back effect occurs in strong magnetic fields where orbital (L) and spin (S) angular momenta decouple.
The energy shift is given by Delta E = \mu_B B (m_l + 2m_s).
Selection rules are delta m_l = 0, +-1 and delta m_s = 0.
The complex anomalous Zeeman pattern transitions into a simpler triplet-like pattern under extreme magnetic fields.
